name: Angola
summary_text: Angola demands real caution from trans visitors. The 2020 Penal Code decriminalised same-sex conduct AND prohibited discrimination based on sexual orientation — one of Africa's stronger statutory packages on paper. A 2024 shadow report by Angolan LGBT organisations (Arquivo de Identidade Angolano, IRIS Angola, Movimento T and others) documents the gap: discrimination persists across health, education and employment; trans people have no legal gender recognition; and violence goes under-investigated. Luanda has a visible, organised community.

sources.claim_summary: Shadow report to the African Commission (81st session, Oct-Nov 2024) by Angolan LGBTIQ organisations (AIA, IRIS Angola, I am Trans Movement, Movimento T, Queer People Alliance of Sex Workers, others) with Synergia and ILGA Pan-Africa. Documents discrimination and stigma, violence, barriers to healthcare including gender-affirming care, and obstacles to access to justice for LGBTQI+ people in Angola, with recommendations to the government.

Submission by Angolan organisations (Arquivo de Identidade Angolano, IRIS Angola, others) to the UN Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (74th pre-session). Addresses discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, barriers LGBT people face in accessing sexual and reproductive health, comprehensive sexuality education, gender-affirming care and education, and the lack of government-generated data on LGBT people in Angola.

SALC chapter 'Transgender Rights in Angola' (Laws and Policies Affecting Transgender Persons in Southern Africa): constitutional rights mapping (Article 23 does not list gender/SO as prohibited discrimination grounds, but 'other status' should be read to include them per UN Human Rights Committee); no specific law for gender-marker change, though section 87 of the 2015 Civil Registration Code gives the registrar general authority to alter records; employment discrimination prohibited under the 2015 Labour Law.

sources.title: LGBTQ+ Rights Are Changing Across Africa. But It's a Thorny Process
sources.claim_summary: VICE (Oct 2019): overview of changing LGBTQ+ rights across Africa - 34 of 54 countries criminalise homosexuality; discusses the 'white person's problem' framing used to dismiss queer rights in Nigeria and the thorny, contested nature of legal change (context including Angola and Botswana).

sources.title: Transsexual artist Titica takes Angola by storm - BBC News
sources.claim_summary: BBC (April 2012): trans kuduro artist Titica takes Angola by storm - a trans woman singer/dancer who is the face of Angola's popular rap-techno fusion, named best kuduro artist 2011, performing at the presidential Divas concert - notable visibility for a trans person in a country where homosexuality was then illegal.

sources.title: Angola decriminalised same-sex sexual relationships
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Feb 2021): Angola decriminalised homosexuality - the new penal code (adopted January 2019, effective February 2021) removed the Portuguese-colonial 'vice against nature' ban and introduced anti-discrimination protection, with discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation punishable by prison.
